summary: DNR lookout above Cle Elum: L-4 cab built 1951, DNR live-in cab on a concrete base 1974, removed 1996; part of the structure now sits in a communications building.

facts.design: L-4 cab (1951), then a DNR live-in cab on a 10-foot concrete block base (1974)
facts.status_note: Cab removed in 1996; a small portion is part of a communications structure on the point

access.note: A yellow gate on the access road may be locked (Willhite); the point now holds communication buildings. Level is our reading of the gate and the communications use, not a posted rule

visit.trail_note: Willhite: drive-up or under a mile, with a gate just under a mile from the lookout; if locked, walk the road. A 2022 trip report found the road ends at a yellow gate, about a half-mile walk to the point

events.note: Three miles of road built to reach a proposed lookout
L-4 cab built, per the register, firelookout.com and Willhite
Forest Lookouts says a 14x14-foot ground house was built as a replacement lookout that year; this conflicts with the L-4 cab account
DNR live-in cab on a 10-foot concrete block base
Register says removed by DNR; firelookout.com says ordered destroyed; Forest Lookouts says the remaining portion became a communications building
Registered August 15, 2012 as US 1376, WA 276; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, firelookout.com and Willhite say an L-4 cab was built in 1951. Forest Lookouts says a 14x14-foot ground house replaced the lookout that year. The story reports both.
The register and Forest Lookouts say removed in 1996; firelookout.com says ordered destroyed. The year agrees; the story uses removed and mentions the order.
Willhite puts the gate just under a mile from the lookout. The 2022 trip report puts the walk from the yellow gate at about half a mile. The story gives both without choosing.

notes_for_editor: Brief kind is two_story: the sources describe a 1951 L-4 cab (or a 14x14-foot ground house) and a 1974 live-in cab on a 10-foot concrete base, and do not use the word two-story. Brief status gone understates the surviving small portion in the communications building; status_note covers it. Access level restricted is our reading of a gate that may be locked plus the communications use; no official access statement was found. No staffing or fire records were found.
